subject: Compliance billing: phased surcharge + implementation-credit roadmap
messages:
From: Maria Espinoza <maria.espinoza@asterhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@asterhealth.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Redwood compliance add-ons — billing phasing question

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for the call yesterday — AsterHealth is excited about moving forward with Redwood, but procurement has one open question we need to close before we can issue an LOI. We want clarity on how the proposed compliance add-on (audit logs + KMS/HSM residency + HIPAA support) will be billed for a pilot -> production ramp.

Specifically: can Redwood provide a model where implementation / evidence delivery fees are either (a) one-time and invoiced up front, or (b) amortized over 12 months as a monthly credit against recurring charges? Our finance team prefers the amortization but legal is worried about long tail commitments.

Also: if we start in US-hosted region and later require EU residency for a subset of data, how do you recommend structuring the surcharge vs the recurring residency fee? Any example amortization schedules or milestone-linked crediting you can share would be helpful.

Can you send a short proposal we can include in the LOI appendix? We attached our standard procurement checklist for reference.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Espinoza
Senior Procurement Manager, AsterHealth
procurement@asterhealth.com

Attachments: Aster_Procurement_Checklist.pdf
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Maria Espinoza <maria.espinoza@asterhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 12:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Redwood compliance add-ons — billing phasing question

Hi Maria — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear ask. Below is a concise option set that maps to tradeoffs we typically see. I'll attach a worked example (spreadsheet) in my follow-up.

Option A — Upfront implementation fee + recurring residency
- One-time implementation / evidence delivery fee that covers work to configure KMS/HSM integrations, attestation artifacts, and audit-log piping.
- Residency surcharge billed monthly once region pivot occurs.
- Pros: clean cut for accounting; Redwood shoulders ongoing operational SLA.
- Cons: larger initial cash outlay for Aster.

Option B — Amortized implementation credit (recommended for pilots)
- Redwood invoices implementation fee up front, but provides a monthly credit spread over 12 months against recurring invoice (visible line-item: Implementation Credit).
- If Aster terminates before 12 months, remaining credit is pro-rated (reduces refund exposure).
- Pros: lower effective TCO during ramp; aligns incentives for timely evidence delivery.
- Cons: extends Redwood's revenue recognition window.

Residency pivot (US -> EU)
- Two levers: residency surcharge (recurring) and data-migration/validation one-time charge.
- We can offer an escalator approach: 0-6 months post-go-live: residency surcharge at 50% list while we stage mirrors; 6+ months: full residency surcharge. Alternatively we can lock residency pricing in the LOI and defer activation until cutover.

Milestone-linked credits (hybrid approach)
- Example: 40% implementation fee up front, 60% amortized across 12 months but tied to evidence milestones (attestation delivered, HSM keys rotated into customer KMS, audit-query baseline completed). If milestones miss target dates, credit schedule pauses until remediation.

Next steps: I'll circulate a short SOW sketch + an amortization worksheet. Can you confirm Aster's preferred accounting treatment (upfront vs amortize) and whether we should include EU-residency as an optional line in the LOI appendix?

—Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: AsterHealth crediting approach — pricing carve-ups

Markus / Ben — quick internal note before we send the worksheet to Maria. Key points I think we should bake in based on win probability and precedent: 
- Use hybrid milestone-crediting by default for pilots (reduces sticker shock at PO stage).
- Keep implementation fee visible (no backdoor bundling) — procurement teams need a clear number.
- Limit Redwood liability: if customer terminates within first 6 months, recoup unamortized credits pro rata. After 6 months, credits convert to non-refundable.
- For EU pivot, propose a default 60-day staging period where residency surcharge is 50% of list to reflect migration effort.

Ben, can you run the numbers on a $250k implementation fee scenario with 12-month amortization vs 6-month amortization (spreadsheet attached). Tessa, please confirm this aligns with our current crediting policy language in the master services agreement. I'll then send a clean appendix to Maria with examples.

Laura
From: Maria Espinoza <maria.espinoza@asterhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Jack Liu <jack.liu@asterhealth.com>, procurement@asterhealth.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood compliance add-ons — billing phasing question

Hi Markus — this is really helpful, thank you. Aster would prefer the hybrid milestone-crediting approach you outlined (pilot: amortize 12 months with milestone gates). We also want the LOI to include an optional EU residency line item with clear activation steps and a capped migration window.

Two asks before we finalize the LOI:
1) Can you send the spreadsheet with the $250k worked example and both 6/12 month amortizations? (Ben was copied earlier)
2) Can you confirm the documentation Redwood will provide as evidence (list of attestation artifacts + delivery SLAs)?

If we get those by Wednesday EOD, procurement can prep the LOI and give legal the appendix to expedite sign-off.

Thanks — Maria
